title: Repository instructions for agents
summary: Keep project instructions short and specific. Share a root AGENTS.md where the chosen host supports it, and verify how that host loads additional guidance.

sections.label: What the file is
sections.text: AGENTS.md is plain Markdown at the repository root with no required fields. The agents.md site calls it a README for agents and lists Codex, Copilot, Cursor and Gemini CLI as readers. Claude Code recommends under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. This practice uses that as an editorial target, not a universal limit or proven optimum.

sections.label: What to put in it
items: Commands to build, test and lint.
Repository structure an agent cannot infer quickly.
Conventions that differ from tool defaults.
Boundaries as always, ask first and never.
Only what the README does not say.

sections.label: What to leave out
sections.text: Keep instructions focused on details the agent cannot reliably discover. Claude Code's /doctor checkup proposes trimming discoverable codebase summaries while retaining pitfalls, rationale and unusual conventions. In the benchmark settings tested, repository overviews did not improve navigation. Claude Code recommends skills for task procedures and path scoped rules for guidance relevant to only part of the codebase.

sections.label: How hosts read it
sections.text: Codex loads global guidance and then at most one instruction file per directory from the project root to the working directory. AGENTS.override.md precedes AGENTS.md, with configured fallback names afterward. The default combined limit is 32 KiB. GitHub's Copilot on GitHub documentation supports AGENTS.md files within the repository, with the nearest file taking precedence. This is not evidence that every Copilot surface and version reads them identically. Claude Code direct AGENTS.md loading needs v2.1.277 or later and an enabled supporting session. Its default chooses CLAUDE.md files when those or CLAUDE.local.md exist on the project path. The Project instructions setting can change that behavior, and a CLAUDE.md can import @AGENTS.md. Use documented host loading or import rules, a plain Markdown link alone does not guarantee inclusion.

sections.label: What the evidence says
sections.text: The reviewed arXiv v3 study tested particular coding agents on SWE-bench and CTXbench. The authors report a 2.4 percent average CTXbench resolution improvement with developer files and average resolution drops of 0.5 and 2 percent with generated files. None of those differences from no context file were statistically significant. Generated files increased average cost by 20 and 23 percent. Removing testing text reduced cost without a significant accuracy change in the reported ablation. File length showed no clear dependency with success or cost. The authors recommend including only what agents need that existing documentation lacks. These results do not establish a universal file length or justify skipping project tests.

sections.label: What Atlas provides
sections.text: The full pack contains an AGENTS.md written from project.json with purpose, commands, workflow, roles, skills, acceptance, boundaries and practices sections. It says it does not run anything, configure an integration or grant a permission. Selecting this practice adds its label and application to the Practices section and records its sources in SOURCES.md.

sections.label: Check in your environment
sections.text: Confirm the host, version and instruction files actually loaded. Check each listed command in the intended environment. A failure can reveal a real defect or missing access, so record and investigate it rather than deleting a valid check. Claude Code v2.1.283 or later supports /doctor prompt-audit for instruction files including AGENTS.md, when its bundled audit skill is enabled. It reports findings without applying changes. Claude Code treats instruction files as context rather than enforced configuration. Its settings and appropriate hooks provide enforcement mechanisms.

sections.label: Review scope
sections.text: Scoped host claims checked on 2026-10-12 against the linked host documentation. Research statements refer to arXiv 2602.11988 v3, not a universal improvement estimate. The content checklist and short file target are editorial recommendations. Host behavior must be confirmed in the intended surface and version.

basis: Scoped host documentation, scoped research findings and proposed practice
confidence: The listed factual claims were checked against their sources on 2026-10-12 within the stated version and host scope. Recommendations and example commands do not prove suitability or execution in a particular project.

catalog.applicability: Use when a repository is worked on by coding agents and needs one shared place for commands, conventions and boundaries.
catalog.limits: The file is written context for an agent. It does not configure a host, grant a permission or prove that its instructions were followed.
